text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple streaming endpoints (SSE/WebSocket proxy) reporting increased tail latency and stalls across us-east-1. p95 ~ 600ms -> 1.2s, p99 spikes > 3s. Possible chunking/buffering issue. Pager triggered to on-call Maya.

Maya (on-call): seeing the alert, joining. I can access the dashboard, p99s are elevated for /v1/generate/stream and /v1/chat/stream. Some clients show stalled SSE frames for 5-10s.

Alex R: confirming on the logs — a lot of upstream slow reads from the runtime hosts. Not obvious CPU/GPU pressure. Network looks fine. Nginx proxy has a lot of connections in keepalive state waiting to flush.

Priya S: is this the same pattern as last month's chunking regress? Could be client backpressure not flushing, or our proxy buffering.

Maya (on-call): quick mitigation checklist: (1) open canary route to fallback model variant (lighter quantized) for streaming (2) disable proxy buffering for SSE/upstream in the ingress (3) increase streaming agent pool briefly. I'll try 2 first.

Maya (on-call): running command to update ingress config (dry-run then apply):
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-ingress patch configmap nginx-ingress -p '{"data":{"proxy_buffering":"off","proxy_read_timeout":"120s","proxy_send_timeout":"120s"}}'
# then rolling restart ingress pods
kubectl -n redwood-ingress rollout restart deployment/nginx-ingress
```

Alex R: FYI I saw nginx error logs with repeated: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and `an upstream response is buffered for too long`. That matches proxy buffering hitting timeouts.

ops-bot: Deploy rollout started for nginx-ingress (3 pods) by Maya.

John L: I'm toggling the per-route chunk flush interval in the streaming gateway to force more frequent flushes (was 2s, set to 200ms) — if client libs expect small frames this may help.

Priya S: Also bumping connection backlog on runtime LB for streaming workers to avoid head-of-line stalls.

Maya (on-call): Noting customer impact: some users see streaming stalls causing perceived timeouts, but most requests eventually complete. No 5xx spike yet, but SLO (p99 latency) breached. Opening incident ticket.

Maya (on-call): Incident ticket: INC-2026-0213 created. Summary: Streaming stalls due to proxy buffering + runtime slow-read. Initial mitigations applied: ingress buffering off + gateway flush interval lowered + scale streaming agents + route to fallback model variant.

Alex R: After ingress patch propagation, immediate reduction in stalled connections on nginx. p95 trending down. p99 still noisy — need to confirm if runtime KV cache stalls during large context lengths.

Maya (on-call): Can someone run the live trace on one of affected requests? Use trace id from logs: `trace=tr_6f8b2a3c` — it's a 35s session where SSE frames stop around 18s.

Priya S: pulled the trace, runtime shows a blocked read in the LLM process waiting on async I/O for ~9s while writing to socket; not GPU bound. Suspect our runtime's socket write path got backpressured by the host TCP buffers.

John L: If the host TCP buffer fills, kernel will block the write syscall until peer reads. That matches client-side slow reads/backpressure. We should add early detection to detect blocked writes and failover or apply small chunk flushing to keep bytes moving.

Maya (on-call): For short-term mitigation we've enabled shorter chunk sizes and forced frequent socket flush. Also temporarily increased runtime write timeout to avoid abrupt disconnects.

Alex R: Customer impact assessment: 8 paying customers had >10% of streaming sessions with visible stalls in last hour. Most are web clients using EventSource polyfills. Recommend proactively notifying top 5 affected accounts.

Maya (on-call): I'll send a coordinated customer message draft for SRE to review. Draft: "We observed intermittent streaming stalls impacting response fluidity; we applied mitigations (ingress buffering disabled, increased flush frequency and scaled streaming workers). We will follow up with root cause and timeline."

Priya S: Ops note — also saw a small bump in backend retransmits from a subset of edge proxies to runtimes; could be intermittent network MTU/fragmentation with specific proxies. We're running connectivity checks to those proxies now.

ops-bot: Connectivity check started for edge proxies in us-east-1. 12/14 passed, 2 showing increased retransmits.

John L: Running a quick script to detect streaming endpoints with slow client ACKs and add a temporary per-client rate limiter to protect runtime from head-of-line blocking.

Alex R: After all mitigations: ingress reload + gateway flush + extra streaming agents + per-client limiter — metrics show p95 back to baseline, p99 improved but still elevated from baseline by ~0.4s. We'll keep monitoring.

Maya (on-call): Handoff: I'll stay on this for the next 30m to confirm stabilization, then pass to Alex for post-incident RCA and rollout of persistent code changes (detect blocked writes, backpressure signals, chunked flush defaults).

Priya S: Noted. For RCA write-up we should capture: nginx buffering defaults, streaming gateway flush policy, runtime socket write behavior under slow client ACKs, and edge proxy retransmit pattern.

Maya (on-call): Postmortem owners: Alex (technical RCA), John (runtime fixes), Priya (network/edge). Target ETA for initial RCA draft: 48 hours.

Maya (on-call): Closing incident channel for now — move to postmortem thread. Leaving incident ticket open until RCA complete. Thanks all ❤️ 

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0213 status updated to "Mitigated" by Maya.

ops-bot: Note: follow-up tasks created: #1234 reduce default chunk interval, #1235 add blocked-write telemetry, #1236 edge proxy health sweep.

Alex R: quick log snippet for trace tr_6f8b2a3c (showing blocked write):
```
[2026-03-13T22:14:12Z] runtime-34 write() 12000 bytes -> blocking for 9003ms waiting on socket
[2026-03-13T22:14:21Z] runtime-34 write() resumed, sent 12000 bytes
[2026-03-13T22:14:21Z] runtime-34 flush() succeeded
```

Priya S: we'll include that in RCA. Good work on the quick mitigations.

Maya (on-call): thanks team. I'll escalate to account CS for the top affected customers now.

John L: leaving a couple of follow-up PRs in flight for chunked flush defaults and adding telemetry for write-block durations.

Maya (on-call): Signing off handoff to Alex in 20m. If it regresses before then page me.

Alex R: Oncall ack. Will take post-incident ownership after Maya signs off.

(End of thread)
